summary: A leaning concrete tower at the end of the San Pedro Breakwater, lit in 1913, with a green flash and a fourth-order lens now in the Los Angeles Maritime Museum.

access.note: Coast Guard aid to navigation at the end of the breakwater; tower closed and breakwater officially closed to the public. Viewable from Cabrillo Beach pier and Point Fermin Park.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NRHP (gale, five days), LighthouseFriends (February 1931 gale, but settling more likely), San Pedro.com (1939 storm) and Trivelli (undocumented; out-of-plumb slab and subsidence) disagree; the story states the disagreement.
NRHP nomination (1977): no personnel since 1971; LighthouseFriends: automated 1 January 1973, last keepers left 30 days later. Roster lists USCG crew at least 1972-1973.
Station was first San Pedro Breakwater Light Station; renamed Los Angeles Harbor Light in 1914 (Trivelli); Angels Gate is a colloquial name.

notes_for_editor: Sources: NRHP nomination, Trivelli (museum director; says the NRHP narrative has errors), LighthouseFriends (facts only), nine Lighthouse Service Bulletin items read in the cached text, WJE and tourism pages. Disagreements: log entry date of the Hughes assault (23 Nov LF, 24 Nov Trivelli); lens range (14 miles LF vs 19 nautical miles Trivelli, not stated in the story); date the lens went to the museum and whether donated or loaned; restoration start Oct 2011 (LF) vs completion Feb 2012 (WJE); lean cause. Bulletin 1922 submarine item: the letter date is OCR'd 'November] 2' and 'yesterday', so the event is 11 November if the letter is dated 12 November; the story says only November 1922. Bulletin pages are PDF pages from the corpus. Roster names are from USLHS; USCG crew entries after 1960 are listed with role crew. LighthouseFriends lists Dean A. Gerberg as head keeper 1962-63 and the head keeper John R. Manyon as 'Mayon'; USLHS lists Gerberg under USCG and 'Manyon'. Newspapers.py search for 1913-14 Chronicling America coverage returned nothing usable. The 'W. Miller' of the 1920 efficiency flag is matched to Willard D. Miller by station and surname (Bulletin prints W. Miller; the 1912-17 index prints 'Miller, W.').
